summary: friendly-greeting-tools ships obfuscated Snowflake credential-exfiltration and file-encryption payloads
details: The package advertises itself as a small greeting utility but src/friendly_greeting/main.py embeds three base64+gzip constants (DEMO_EN, DEMO_ST, DEMO_SC) that a run_demo() helper decodes and passes to exec(). DEMO_ST connects to Snowflake using an OAuth token read from /snowflake/session/token, escalates to ACCOUNTADMIN, creates an external stage bound to s3://pkusinski-external/ via AWS role arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role, and COPY INTOs that stage from ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS, exfiltrating table contents to an attacker-controlled S3 bucket. DEMO_SC reads /snowflake/session/token, /root/.snowflake/connections.toml, /root/.dbt/profiles.yml, and /snowflake/secrets/pip.conf and encrypts them with a hardcoded 2048-bit RSA public key using OAEP-SHA256, producing ciphertexts only the payload author can decrypt. The credential-theft payloads target Snowflake worksheet / Snowpark Container Services credential paths and are wholly unrelated to any greeting functionality; obfuscation via base64+gzip+exec conceals their behavior from casual inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
